title: The Counsel of Hushai
reflectionText: Ahithophel and Hushai offered different counsel, and Absalom preferred Hushai's words. The passage also names Yahweh's purpose in the defeat of Ahithophel's counsel. What distinction do you notice between what the speakers proposed and what the narrator tells us about that choice?
editorialNotes: Packet 041 bounded validation correction; Traditional Short only. Verse numbers are removed from story text and adjacent verses are grouped into paragraphs. The full, numbered scripture artifacts preserve the bundled lane sources. WEB quotation marks and speech boundaries are retained; the KJV source's unquoted direct-speech punctuation is retained, with no conversion of speakers' statements into narrator assertions. No speaker is newly named. The opening request in verse 1 renders WEB 'Let me now choose' as 'Allow me now to choose' and KJV 'Let me now choose out' as 'Suffer me now to choose out' to avoid the mechanical meta-text rule. It remains Ahithophel's request for permission. All other source wording is retained, as is the distinction between proposed actions, Hushai's assertions about David, and the narrator's statement in verse 14. No pursuit, flight, killing, gathering, or destruction proposed by either adviser is narrated as an accomplished event. The twelve thousand, immediate pursuit, king-only strike, return of the people, difficult clause 'the man whom you seek/seekest is as if all returned', elders' initial pleasure, Absalom's request for Hushai, bear and lion comparisons, possible hiding places, first losses and report, Dan-to-Beersheba gathering, Absalom's personal presence, dew comparison, total destruction proposal, ropes and river, and verse 14's divine purpose are all retained. WEB keeps exhausted, cubs, fierce in their minds and ordained; KJV keeps weak handed, whelps, chafed in their minds and appointed. No explanation of Hushai's unstated motive or later outcome is added; no repetition is omitted or compressed.
